data.name: Pooja
data.gender_notes: Pooja is used as a female name in hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit root pūj, 'to worship, honour' — pūjā, 'worship'. Its root is Sanskrit pūj (पूज्). A central Hindu devotional practice. Pooja is a Sanskrit name meaning “Worship; prayer; homage”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.
data.spiritual_meaning: Pooja expresses “Worship; prayer; homage”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.etymology: From the Sanskrit root pūj, 'to worship, honour' — pūjā, 'worship'.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Pooja total 21, reducing to 3. Number 3 is associated with expression, creativity and optimism.

vedic_reference.note: The term Pooja is derived from the Sanskrit word पूजन (pūjana), which means 'to honor, to adore, to worship'. In the Vedas, Pooja is mentioned as an important aspect of connecting with the Divine. For instance, in the Rigveda (10.129.1), it is mentioned that the devas (gods) are pleased with Pooja and offer their blessings to those who perform it.
